newsitem.title: POLAND: Seven investors to apply for Poland's DCS licence.
newsitem.headline: Seven investors to apply for Poland's DCS licence.

text.p: Seven investors are interested in a licence to run a DCS digital mobile telephone system in Poland, the head of the committee which will grant the licence told Reuters by telephone on Friday.
"There are seven possible investors which have already bought tender documents," Marian Dabrowski said.

He said that among the investors was the Polish analogue mobile phone operator Centertel as well as France's Alcatel, Swedish Ericsson, Telecom Finland, the Polish Telecoms monopoly TPSA, Diplomatel International and an undisclosed company represented by Polish KNS Lawyer's Office.

Dabrowski said the licence for DCS system, issued together with a permit to cover the territory of at least 10 Polish provinces, would be granted by the Telecommunications Ministry by mid-September following a public tender.
The deadline for entering the tender is July 14.
The DCS system is a more advanced version of the popular Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) cellular telephone system, using a higher frequency of 1800 Mhz instead of GSM's 900 Mhz.
